title: A protocol for whole-mount immuno-coupled hybridization chain reaction (WICHCR) in zebrafish embryos and larvae
protocol: Reconstitute recently fertilized zebrafish embryos in 1× E3 culture media.
Switch embryos to 0.0045% PTU/E3 solution after 22 hpf.
Incubate embryos at 20°C–25°C without agitation, unless otherwise specified.
Add 100 μL of Pronase stock for dechorionation as early as 16 hpf.
Incubate with Pronase for 30 minutes to facilitate chorion removal.
Rinse embryos three times with 1× E3 culture media after chorions are removed.
Sort and collect previously dechorionated zebrafish embryos/larvae into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 1 mL of freshly thawed 4% PFA per tube to fix samples for approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash samples with 1 mL of 1× PBS three times, each wash lasting five minutes.
Discard the liquid waste according to the PFA handling specifications.
Dehydrate and permeabilize the samples with a series of methanol (MeOH) washes: 100% MeOH for 10 minutes.
Repeat the MeOH wash with 100% MeOH for another 10 minutes.
Store samples at -20°C for approximately 16 hours before use.
Rehydrate tissue with 75% MeOH/ 25% 1× PBST for 5 min.
Rehydrate tissue with 50% MeOH/ 50% 1× PBST for 5 min.
Rehydrate tissue with 25% MeOH/ 75% 1× PBST for 5 min.
Wash tissue twice in 100% 1× PBST for 5 min each.
Incubate samples in pre-chilled acetone at −20°C for 12 min.
Wash samples three times with 1× PBST for 5 min each.
Incubate with 10 μg/mL Proteinase K diluted in 1× PBST, time varies by developmental stage.
Wash samples three times with PBST without incubation.
Fix samples with 4% PFA for 20 min.
Wash samples 5 times for 5 min each with 1 mL of PBST.
Pre-warm probe hybridization buffer to 37°C.
Incubate zebrafish embryos/larvae in the pre-warmed probe hybridization buffer.
Hybridize zebrafish larvae with HCR probe sets against elavl3 and phox2bb for a 3-marker experiment, or sox10, barx1, and mitfa for a 5-marker spectrally deconvolved experiment.
Incubate the samples for 1 hour followed by an overnight incubation at 12-16 hours.
Pre-hybridize samples with 250 μL of probe hybridization buffer for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Thaw all the HCR probe sets that will be used for the experiment while the samples are pre-hybridizing.
Prepare HCR probe mixture solution by adding 2–3 pmol of each probe set into 250 μL of probe hybridization buffer.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Pre-warm the probe mixture solution at 37°C for 15 minutes before adding to the samples.
Replace pre-hybridization solution with probe mixture solution and incubate the samples for 12–16 hours at 37°C.
Remove unbound HCR probes and initiate HCR signal amplification by choosing the correct amplifier for the desired wavelength.
Wash excess probe 4 times for 15 min each with 250 μL of pre-warmed probe wash buffer at 37°C.
Label tube containing probe mixture solution with probe sets used and number of times used.
Wash larvae 2 times for 5 min each with 500 μL 5× SSCT.
Pre-amplify larvae with 250 μL of 20°C–25°C probe amplification buffer for 30 min.
Thaw all the amplifier hairpins that will be used for the experiment while the samples are pre-amplifying.
Add 3–5 μL of the first amplifier hairpin h1 (3 μM stocks) in a sterile tube for each tissue condition.
In a separate tube, add an equal volume of amplifier hairpin h2.
Label each tube with the corresponding hairpin number and B isoform.
Carefully note the detection wavelength for each tube.
Heat all amplifier hairpin tubes at 95°C for 90 seconds.
Let the heated tubes cool to 20°C–25°C in a dark drawer for 30 minutes.
Prepare amplifier hairpin mixture solution by adding snap cooled h1 and h2 hairpins to 250 μL of amplification buffer per tissue condition.
Replace pre-amplification buffer with amplifier hairpin mixture solution, adding 250 μL per tube.
Incubate all samples for 12–16 h at 20°C–25°C protected from light.
Wash excess amplifier hairpins by washing with successive 5× SSCT as follows: Perform 2 washes of 5 min each.
Perform 2 additional washes of 30 min each.
Wash tissue with 5× SSCT for 5 minutes.
Wash tissue with 1× PBST three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Check fluorescence under a fluorescence macroscope to confirm correct HCR pattern.
Visually confirm that HCR signal is detectable before proceeding further.
Minimize exposure of tissue to high intensity lasers to reduce photobleaching.
Proceed directly to step 36 if validating a new HCR probe for the first time in wild-type tissue without completing the antibody detection step.
Dispense 5% goat block solution to samples and incubate for 1–2 hours at 20°C–25°C or for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Select animal serum based on the specific antibody combinations to be used.
Use sterile technique when handling animal serums to prevent bacterial contamination.
Prepare primary antibody solution by diluting antibodies with confirmed working concentration in block solution.
Remove blocking solution and replace with diluted primary antibody solution.
Incubate tissue with primary antibody solution for approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash excess primary antibody six times, each wash lasting 30 minutes with 1× PBST.
Prepare secondary antibody solution by diluting corresponding secondary antibodies in block solution.
Incubate samples in secondary antibody solution for approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Perform optimizations for concentration, incubation time, and primary antibody compatibility prior to starting a WICHCR protocol.
Add volume of antibody solution between 100–500 μL per tissue condition to cover embryos.
Wash out excess secondary antibody 6 x 30 min with 1× PBST.
Check antibody and HCR signal under a fluorescence macroscope to confirm retained HCR signal and correct antibody staining.
Cover samples with foil and store in a dark drawer during incubations to reduce photobleaching.
Clear embryos in serial glycerol solutions at 20°C–25°C by sequentially adding 500 μL of:
25% glycerol/75% 1× PBST
50% glycerol/50% 1× PBST
75% glycerol/25% 1× PBST
Mount embryos in 75% glycerol/ 25% 1× PBST for imaging.
Image using the settings required to capture the signal in the regions of interest.
Process and analyze the data according to the experimental outline using image analysis software.
